Design the complete PearlOS user flow for: Notes → Launchpad → Output experience.

2. Pearl responds: "Want a design document or go straight to production?"

ANALYZE:
1. Pearl's conversation flow — when to offer design doc vs direct build?
2. Notes app integration — how does Pearl populate the first draft?
3. Magic wand button mechanics — what triggers the Launchpad handoff?
4. Document parsing — how does Launchpad interpret the design doc?
5. Output lifecycle — where do built artifacts live? How are they versioned?

content.Text:
# PearlOS User Journey: Notes → Launchpad → Output

## 1. Pearl's Conversation Flow

**Decision Tree:**

```
User: "I want to make a space invaders 80s arcade game with roguelike elements"
                            │
                Pearl classifies intent
                            │
              ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
              │             │             │
         Ambiguous      Complex       Simple/Clear
         (explore)    (needs design)   (just build)
              │             │             │
      "Tell me more    "Want a design   "On it. Opening
       about what       doc first, or    Launchpad now."
       you're           go straight to
       imagining"       production?"
                            │
                    ┌───────┴───────┐
                    │               │
               Design Doc      Direct Build
                    │               │
              Opens Notes      Opens Launchpad
              with draft       with build spec
```

**When to offer design doc vs direct build:**

| Signal | Route |
|--------|-------|
| Multi-system project (game with roguelike + arcade mechanics) | Design doc |
| Creative/artistic intent ("80s arcade feel") | Design doc — needs aesthetic decisions |
| Single well-defined output ("make me a calculator") | Direct build |
| User has built before / says "just do it" | Direct build |
| Ambiguous scope ("something fun") | Clarify first, then decide |

Pearl's heuristic: **If the project has more than 2 design dimensions (mechanics, aesthetics, systems, content), default to design doc.**

---

## 2. Notes App Integration — First Draft Population

When Pearl routes to Notes, she doesn't just open a blank doc. She writes a structured first draft:

```
Pearl → Notes App
  │
  ├── Creates new Note (type: "design-document")
  ├── Populates via server action (notes feature)
  ├── Structure:
  │     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │     │ 🎮 Space Invaders Roguelike     │
  │     │                                 │
  │     │ ## Vision                        │
  │     │ 80s arcade aesthetic with        │
  │     │ roguelike progression...         │
  │     │                                 │
  │     │ ## Core Mechanics               │
  │     │ - Wave-based shooting           │
  │     │ - Permadeath with meta-progress │
  │     │ - Procedural enemy patterns     │
  │     │                                 │
  │     │ ## Tech Stack                   │
  │     │ Engine: Godot 4                 │
  │     │ Style: Pixel art, CRT shader   │
  │     │                                 │
  │     │ ## Open Questions               │
  │     │ - Power-up system depth?        │
  │     │ - Leaderboard / local only?     │
  │     │                                 │
  │     │         ┌──────────┐            │
  │     │         │ 🪄 Build │            │
  │     │         └──────────┘            │
  │     └─────────────────────────────────┘
  │
  └── Pearl says: "Opened a design doc in Notes.
       Edit it however you want, then hit
       the wand when it feels right."
```

**Integration mechanism:**
- Pearl emits `notes.document.create` event with structured content
- Notes feature receives via event handler, creates the document
- Document is a content type stored via Prism (not raw storage)
- Pearl can continue chatting while user edits — conversational context preserved

---

## 3. Magic Wand Button Mechanics

The wand button is the bridge between **design** (Notes) and **execution** (Launchpad).

```
User clicks 🪄 in Notes
        │
        ▼
  Notes packages the document
        │
        ├── Extracts structured sections (vision, mechanics, tech stack)
        ├── Serializes as LaunchSpec JSON
        │     {
        │       "type": "game",
        │       "engine": "godot",
        │       "title": "Space Invaders Roguelike",
        │       "designDoc": "<full markdown>",
        │       "extractedSpec": {
        │         "mechanics": [...],
        │         "aesthetic": "80s-arcade-crt",
        │         "platform": "desktop"
        │       }
        │     }
        │
        ▼
  Emits event: `launchpad.build.request`
        │
        ▼
  Launchpad receives, opens build view
        │
        ├── Shows build plan preview (user can confirm/adjust)
        ├── "Pearl will handle the rest. Estimated: ~3 min"
        └── Build begins
```

**Key UX detail:** The wand doesn't silently fire. It shows a brief confirmation:

> "Send this to Launchpad for building?"
> [Cancel] [🪄 Build It]

This prevents accidental triggers on incomplete docs.

---

## 4. Document Parsing — How Launchpad Interprets the Design Doc

Launchpad doesn't parse markdown headings with regex. It uses Pearl (the AI layer) to interpret:

```
LaunchSpec JSON arrives at Launchpad
        │
        ▼
  Launchpad routes by `type` field
        │
        ├── "game"    → Godot pipeline
        ├── "webapp"  → Web build pipeline  
        ├── "script"  → Direct execution
        └── "unknown" → Pearl classifies
        
        │
        ▼
  Pipeline receives full designDoc + extractedSpec
        │
        ├── Agency (AI build team) reads the design doc
        ├── Decomposes into build tasks:
        │     1. Project scaffold (Godot project structure)
        │     2. Core mechanics (player, enemies, waves)
        │     3. Roguelike systems (permadeath, upgrades)
        │     4. Art/audio (pixel sprites, CRT shader, chiptune)
        │     5. Polish (menus, scores, game feel)
        │
        ├── Each task assigned to appropriate agent
        └── Progress streams back to Launchpad UI
```

**The design doc is a conversation, not a config file.** Pearl/Agency reads it like a human would — understanding intent, filling gaps with reasonable defaults, asking the user only when genuinely ambiguous.

---

## 5. Output Lifecycle — Artifacts, Versioning, Access

```
Build completes
        │
        ▼
  Artifact stored via Prism
        │
        ├── Content type: "launchpad-artifact"
        ├── Metadata:
        │     {
        │       "title": "Space Invaders Roguelike",
        │       "type": "game",
        │       "engine": "godot",
        │       "version": 1,
        │       "sourceDocId": "note-abc123",
        │       "buildId": "build-xyz789",
        │       "status": "ready"
        │     }
        │
        ▼
  Appears in Launchpad menu
        │
        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
        │  🎮 Space Invaders Roguelike │
        │  v1 · Built 2 min ago        │
        │                              │
        │  [✏️ Edit]    [🚀 Launch]    │
        └──────────────────────────────┘
        
  Edit → Routes back to Agency
        │
        ├── Opens with context: original design doc + current build
        ├── User describes changes conversationally
        ├── Agency patches (doesn't rebuild from scratch)
        └── New version: v2 (v1 still accessible)
        
  Launch → Starts instantly
        │
        ├── Game: Opens in embedded player or native window
        ├── Web app: Opens in browser/mini-browser
        └── Script: Executes in terminal feature
```

**Versioning model:**
- Each build creates a new version (immutable)
- Edit always creates v(n+1), never mutates v(n)
- User can roll back: "Go back to v1" via Pearl or Launchpad UI
- Source design doc maintains link to all versions it spawned

---

## Complete Journey Map

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        USER JOURNEY                             │
│                                                                 │
│  CONVERSATION          NOTES              LAUNCHPAD             │
│  ───────────          ─────              ─────────              │
│                                                                 │
│  "I want to make     ┌──────────┐                               │
│   a space invaders   │          │                               │
│   roguelike"         │...
